failures: Q01 (3/10): Marks the commission rep (a) as a violation by claiming 'the owner's constraint implies no third-party calling either,' then removes the rep from the corrected plan.
Q02 (3/10): Brokerage revenue is computed as '$70 referral fee per device' when $70 is the subcontract cost; margin should be $25-$80.
Q03 (3/10): Classifies S3 as SUPPORTED by claiming the 9 serviced listings 'sold for an average of $1,850', which F4 never says, and in the same cell admits no price comparison exists.
Q04 (5/10): Calls restaurant collection fees 'not confirmed by the facts' and rejects compliance reporting as revenue, so it misses the core model the key requires.
Q05 (1/10): Says the owner cannot operate at all because 500 units need $9,125 at day 35, wrongly adding $14.50 per unit of receivables to costs already paid.
Q06 (6/10): The 'what would change' section is wrong: it says ~87 beds and ~14 beds/week using a nonsensical $703.33 cost, when 90 beds (6 more) are needed.
Q07 (1/10): States 'The owner signs the certification statement', which has the English-only owner falsely attest to Portuguese translation competence.
Q08 (4/10): Treats C's $1,700 working capital as an expense ($8,100 - $1,700 = $6,400), which understates the best strategy and the combined total ($12,054).

Q09 (6/10): Does not recognize that the business's market includes unknown municipal-utility applications, omits the municipal utility's unknown fee, and leaves S6's validity vague ('provide context').
Q10 (2/10): Asserts the 'Owner must pay subcontractor 15 days before receiving payment from fleet' despite net-45 payables versus net-30 receivables, which wrongly validates C5.
Q11 (0/10): Its calendar arithmetic is wrong from T2 onward, so it reports a baseline delivery of Dec 19 (late), a scenario (c) delivery of Dec 26, and then recommends paying the mill $700.
Q12 (2/10): Marks O5 as failing constraint 5 because a farmers market booth supposedly makes the address public, and misses O1's tobacco violation entirely.
Q13 (6/10): It rates E1 and E5 as PARTLY SUPPORTS, treating search curiosity and one competitor's revenue rise as partial support for strong paying demand and a 20% premium.

Q14 (4/10): Ranks verification of the already-stated net-60 terms as the second most decision-relevant question, while omitting recycler capacity and subcontracting, contract term and exclusivity, and pallet ownership.

Q15 (3/10): It invents fee-free selling and computes shipping as $140/8 while projecting 4-panel shipments, so the recomputed economics are internally wrong; it also never discloses the missing UL label to buyers.
Q17 (4/10): Computes $662.50 ÷ $186.50 ≈ 3.55 but labels it 'calls/day' and '~107 calls/month', then contradicts itself by calling 12.5 calls/month profitable.
Q18 (4/10): The capacity calculation '$5,400 ÷ ($312.50 × 30 days)' is dimensionally nonsensical and rests on a misread 50% subcontractor cost, giving an unsupported 6-8 jobs.
Q19 (2/10): Claims '31 current customers + 14 new conversions = 45 stores' by treating competitors' customers as already won, and ignores the 30-store minimum entirely.

Q20 (1/10): Buys only a 20-ton minimum by Nov 1 but projects selling 312 tons with $1,386 profit and a $14,940 peak capital need. Its cost lines actually sum to $52,654, not $51,654, so profit is about $386, and the plan ignores the $28.7k needed to prepay 312 t.
Q21 (5/10): It says the clinic 'loses $2 per hour' at $70, when $72 reimbursed minus $70 is a $2 gain.
Q22 (0/10): It bills 3.6 weeks and 1.8 months of rental within 18 rented days and omits delivery costs, concluding a single machine earns $15,769 in peak and $5,720 in winter.

Q23 (3/10): Says the import order needs only $19,000, which it claims 'exceeds $20,000', omitting tariff and freight cash, and then calls domestic capital 'minimal' while proposing 4,000-5,000 pay-on-order units.

Q24 (4/10): Resolves A vs B with an impossible subset claim and simply prefers 4,850, so the discrepancy is effectively left unexplained; it also omits the dollar floor and the disposal and licensing questions.
Q25 (1/10): Concludes the standard COI delivered at 5 p.m. meets a 2 p.m. deadline, and that X is cleared by March 5, with 6 cleaners required.

Q26 (5/10): It says 10-15% capture is achievable 'given the thin competition among mobile agents', which re-imports the memo's unsupported thin-competition claim, and it gives only a single-point market estimate at a miscomputed midpoint fee.
Q27 (2/10): Shows a median sale netting -$2, then concludes only 2.1 sales/month are needed for $5,000 net, which contradicts its own loss figure.

Q28 (3/10): It caps option 3 at 83 jobs by treating ad spend as unfunded capital, ignoring the booking deposits. It then has profit arriving in late January, so its 'YES' verdict contradicts its own window.
Q29 (1/10): Chooses Q as stronger even though it computes P's profit at more than three times Q's, and justifies this with an impossible $28k upfront purchase.
Q30 (3/10): Peak working capital is stated as $3,600 while 35 clients imply about $14k of monthly crew cost paid weekly against month-end collection, so the cash constraint is badly understated.
